name: Competitive Grants Program
contact: Deb Vaughn, Grants Manager, debv@traveloregon.com; Susanne Falenczykowski, susannef@traveloregon.com
award: 2026 cycle: large-scale track for requests above $500,000 from a $5,000,000 pool (two awards). Earlier cycles funded a wider range of project sizes.
opens: 2027 cycle guidelines expected fall 2026; awards June 2027
match: Required for large-scale requests; ratio not published for 2026.
notes: Ten percent of Travel Oregon's budget funds tourism projects that enhance, expand or promote the visitor industry; the 2025-27 focus is extending the visitor season, raising visitor spending and year-round jobs. The 2026 cycle was a large-scale program (over $500,000 per request) with a letter of intent then invited applications. Eligible applicants are Oregon local governments (not state/federal agencies), port districts, federally recognized tribes and Oregon-registered nonprofits; for-profits cannot apply. The 2027 cycle timeline posted so far is guidelines in fall 2026 and awards in June 2027, so watch for a winter 2027 LOI window.

name: Capacity and Small Project Grants
award: Not published per award; more than $1.4 million awarded program-wide

deadlines.label: 2022 cycle (most recent; no new cycle posted)

opens: No new cycle announced
notes: Capacity-building and small project grants restricted to federally recognized tribes and Oregon destination marketing/management organizations that receive lodging tax (or are recognized by a local government). Event producers are not direct applicants; a local DMO partner would have to apply. The program page says applications are no longer being accepted and no 2026 or 2027 cycle is posted, so treat it as dormant.

name: Oregon Wine Country License Plates Matching Grants
contact: Dawn Smallman, dawns@traveloregon.com; Susanne Falenczykowski, susannef@traveloregon.com
award: Up to $50,000 per project; up to two projects per applicant
opens: 2026 cycle: guidelines Dec 18, 2025, application Jan 20 to Feb 19, 2026; 2027 cycle not yet posted
match: 1:1 match required, at least half in cash
notes: Funds projects that promote wine and/or culinary tourism, including events and marketing. Only 'tourism promotion agencies' as defined in ORS 320.300 may apply (nonprofits or governmental units doing tourism promotion, or associations whose members are mostly tourism businesses); for-profits are not eligible. Pattern is guidelines in December, applications mid-January to mid-February, awards in May. 2024 awards totaled $316,526.

name: Arts Build Communities (ABC) Grant
contact: Tiffany Harker, tiffany.harker@biz.oregon.gov, 971-719-6169; Kat Bell, kat.bell@biz.oregon.gov
award: Typically $5,000 per award (listings show a $1,000 to $10,000 range); roughly $180,000 to $260,000 awarded statewide per year
opens: Usually opens early summer, due in August for the following calendar year
match: Not required; budget must show cash and in-kind contributions
notes: Funds new, arts-based projects that address a local community need, with priority for underserved communities and rural areas; cultural tourism and festivals have been funded. Applicants must be Oregon 501(c)(3) nonprofits, units of local government (including libraries and schools) or tribal governments; fiscally sponsored groups cannot apply and a SAM.gov UEI is required. Recent cycles have been due in mid-August with a January 1 to December 31 project period.

name: Sustaining Arts Program (SAP) Group A, operating support for arts organizations under $150,000
contact: Tiffany Harker, tiffany.harker@biz.oregon.gov, 971-719-6169; Kat Bell, kat.bell@biz.oregon.gov, 971-304-5044
award: $1,000 to $3,000, divided evenly among eligible applicants
opens: Usually opens in spring, due mid-May
notes: Replaces the former Small Operating Grant. Unrestricted operating support for Oregon arts nonprofits with an arts-focused mission, year-round public programming and 501(c)(3) status; fiscally sponsored groups are not eligible. Arts festivals that are organized as arts nonprofits qualify. Expect the FY2028 round to open in spring 2027.

name: Sustaining Arts Program (SAP) Group B, operating support for arts organizations $150,000 and up
contact: Tiffany Harker, tiffany.harker@biz.oregon.gov, 971-719-6169; Kat Bell, kat.bell@biz.oregon.gov, 971-304-5044
award: $5,000 to $25,000, formula-based on organization size; about $1.2 million awarded to roughly 150 organizations per year
opens: Usually opens in spring, due mid-May
notes: Replaces the former Operating Support and Arts Services grants. For Oregon arts nonprofits with cash operating expenses of at least $150,000 on the most recent IRS 990, a SAM.gov UEI, year-round public programming and 501(c)(3) status. Organizations housed within a larger nonprofit, university or tribe can request an eligibility waiver.

name: Cultural Development Grants
contact: Aili Schreiner, 503-428-0963, Aili.Schreiner@biz.oregon.gov; Raissa Fleming, Raissa.Fleming@biz.oregon.gov
opens: Guidelines usually posted in February; due first week of May; FY2028 cycle not yet posted
match: At least 1:1 match in cash or eligible in-kind
notes: Four categories: Access to Culture, Cultural Heritage and Preservation, Cultural Creativity, and Strengthen Cultural Capacity. Open to Oregon cultural nonprofits on the Trust's eligible list (apply to join the list first), tribal cultural entities and colleges with significant cultural programs; fiscal sponsorship is not allowed and for-profits cannot apply. Events whose main purpose is fundraising for non-cultural causes are excluded. Awards are notified in August after the state budget is enacted.

name: Organizational and Professional Development Grants
award: Up to $2,500 (organizational development) or $1,000 (professional development)
opens: Accepted on a rolling basis within the Nov 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027 activity period
notes: Small capacity grants for Oregon cultural nonprofits and county/tribal cultural coalitions with operating budgets under $1.5 million: strategic planning, board training, consultants, conference attendance. Not for producing events, but useful for festival organizations building capacity. Applications accepted on a rolling basis with two review deadlines.

name: Oregon Heritage Grant
funder: Oregon Heritage (Oregon Parks and Recreation Department)
award: Generally $3,000 to $20,000; $380,000 pool in the 2025-27 biennium
opens: Applications open late August 2027 for the 2027-29 biennium
match: Grant covers no more than 50% of project cost; up to half of applicant share may be in-kind
notes: One cycle per biennium for projects that preserve, develop or interpret Oregon heritage: exhibits, oral histories, public education events, theatrical performances, films, teaching traditional practices and heritage interpretation. Eligible applicants are Oregon 501(c)(3) nonprofits, tribal governments, colleges and local governments; for-profits, individuals and religious organizations cannot apply. Reimbursement-based; the next cycle opens late August 2027 with a fall 2027 deadline.

name: Oregon Museum Grant
funder: Oregon Heritage (Oregon Parks and Recreation Department)
award: Generally $1,000 to $8,000
opens: Applications open late January 2027; 2027 deadline to be announced
match: Not required; local cash, in-kind and volunteer time make applications more competitive
notes: For Oregon public and nonprofit museums open at least 120 hours a year and operating for two years. Funds collections care, heritage tourism, and heritage education and interpretation projects, which can include exhibits and programs. Annual pattern is a late-January opening and early-April deadline with a July 1 project start.

name: Public Program Grants
award: Up to $5,000; $100,002 awarded to 25 organizations in 2026

deadlines.label: 2026 round closed in spring 2026 (exact date not posted; round is closed)

opens: Typically opens early in the calendar year and closes in early to mid spring; 2027 dates not posted
match: 1:1 match required; grant may be no more than 50% of program budget
notes: Funds humanities-based public programs such as community dialogues, culturally specific celebrations, storytelling and history programs (a Juneteenth celebration is a listed example). Cannot pay for creating or performing art. Open to Oregon 501(c)(3) nonprofits with budgets under $1.5 million and federally recognized tribes; no fiscal sponsors; SAM.gov UEI required. The 2026 round is closed; sign up for notices for the 2027 window.

name: Community Grants Program
contact: Regional offices: Portland 503-227-6846, Bend 541-382-1170, Eugene 541-431-7099, Medford 541-773-8987, Salem 503-779-1927, Baker City 541-665-8626
award: Not published per award; Spring 2027 cycle is general operating support
notes: OCF's largest open program, with Arts and Culture and Community Engagement among its impact areas. The Spring 2027 cycle (RFP released Nov 2, 2026, applications Nov 17 to Dec 15, 2026, awards late April 2027) provides general operating support. Organizations that received a Community Grant in 2026 must sit out this cycle. Fall cycles typically open in late summer; the Small Arts and Culture Grants were folded into the Arts and Culture Rebuilding Program, which is not currently accepting applications.

name: Creative Heights
award: $10,000 to $100,000; up to $1 million awarded annually

deadlines.label: 2026 invited full application, May 2026 (exact day not posted)

opens: Letter of inquiry window reopens January 2027
notes: Funds the creation and presentation of new, innovative performances, exhibitions and cultural works led by Oregon artists and culture bearers, with artists paid professionally. Individuals and collectives need a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor at the full-application stage. Two-step process: LOI in February, invited applications due in May, awards in August, two-year spending window. Not for routine repeats of existing festivals; the work must show creative evolution.

name: Oregon Historic Trails Fund
award: Not published
opens: 2026 window was Sept 1 to Oct 15; 2027 not posted
notes: Supports interpretive, educational and economic development projects along Oregon's designated historic trails (Oregon Trail, Applegate, Barlow Road and others). Relevant to heritage events and commemorations along trail corridors. Annual fall window.

name: Project Support Grants
award: Up to $200,000 per year for up to two years
opens: 2027 cycle not yet posted
notes: Meyer funds projects advancing racial, social and economic justice through four portfolios (Our Resilient Places, Our Empowered Youth, Our Collective Prosperity, Together We Rise). Culturally specific festivals and arts projects can fit when framed around community power and belonging, but general tourism or entertainment events do not. Fiscally sponsored projects, government and tribal entities are eligible. The former Community Small Grants program is discontinued.

name: GO Grants (formerly Responsive Grantmaking)
award: Not published; 2024 median grant about $40,000 (209 grants, $10.75 million)
opens: Start with the Partnership Alignment Screener on the foundation website at any time
notes: General operating and project grants to Oregon nonprofits in arts and culture, education, environment, health equity and quality of life, with an equity emphasis. Requires at least one year of operation, a $20,000 minimum budget, four independent board members and a nondiscrimination policy; fiscally sponsored projects may qualify. Primarily sports programs are excluded. Process begins with an online screener rather than a fixed deadline.

name: Good Neighbor Grants (and Open Oregon larger requests)

geography.region: Rural Oregon communities under about 35,000 population not adjacent to metro areas, plus Siskiyou County, California

award: Up to $20,000 (Good Neighbor); up to $5,000 technical assistance; requests above $20,000 (Open Oregon) require contacting staff first
opens: Applications are always open
match: At least 25% of project cost committed before applying (in-kind counts); grant covers up to one-third of program costs or 50% of capital
notes: One of the few Oregon funders that explicitly lists free multi-day or annual community events such as music or art series, celebrations and summer festivals as an eligible use. Serves rural-serving 501(c)(3) nonprofits and public entities in rural Oregon and Siskiyou County, California; for-profits cannot apply. Rolling applications; decisions typically within a few months. Larger Open Oregon requests must align with foundation priorities and start with a staff conversation.

name: Autzen Foundation Grants

geography.region: Oregon (and limited southwest Washington)

award: Typically $1,000 to $25,000; 2024 median $5,000 (305 grants, $1.82 million)
opens: Deadlines not published; one request per 12 months; winter cycle eliminated
notes: Longtime Portland-based funder of social services, arts and culture, education, environment and youth programs across Oregon. Organizations must have been tax-exempt for at least two years; fiscally sponsored groups, individuals, multi-year requests and fundraising events are not eligible. Arts programming and festivals with an arts mission have been funded; check the foundation's current cycle before applying.

name: Jackson Foundation Grants
contact: Contact page at thejacksonfoundation.com; 17650 NE Sandy Blvd, Portland, OR 97230 (no phone calls)

geography.region: Portland area favored; statewide projects considered if they have statewide appeal

award: $1,000 to $50,000; historical average about $3,400
opens: Accepted continuously; reviewed at quarterly trustee meetings
notes: Broad-purpose charitable fund that must 'promote the welfare of the public of the City of Portland or the State of Oregon.' Grants are small and quarterly; applications received after a quarter-end deadline roll to the next meeting. No grants to individuals, private businesses or (generally) K-12 schools, and generally one grant per organization per 12 months.

name: Oregon Grant Program
contact: 5885 Meadows Rd, Suite 200, Lake Oswego, OR 97035
opens: Annual; 2027 dates not posted (2026 deadline was June 15)
notes: Supports the health, education and welfare of Oregon children and youth under 21 through Oregon-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits. Youth arts programs and youth-focused community events can fit; general festivals do not. Annual cycle with a mid-June deadline in 2026.

name: Open Call Grants

geography.region: Rural Oregon and Tribal communities only (all regions outside the Portland metro core)

award: No published range; Spring 2026 average about $12,800 (125 grants, $1.6 million)
opens: Spring and fall open calls; the fall 2026 window ran June 10 to Aug 14, 2026; spring 2027 dates not posted
notes: Funds rural Oregon and Tribal nonprofits and community governments in four areas including Arts and Culture (performing, visual, media arts). Also runs Small Grants, Capital and Technical Assistance programs. Check for the spring 2027 open call, which in recent years opened in winter.

name: Pacific Power Foundation Grants (Arts and Culture, Community Enhancement, Education, Safety and Wellness cycles)

geography.region: Pacific Power service territory in Oregon (plus parts of Washington and northern California)

deadlines.label: Community Enhancement and Environmental Respect cycle (annual June 15)

opens: Four annual cycles; the arts and culture cycle has typically been awarded in winter (2026 round announced January 2026)
notes: The Arts and Culture cycle funds performing and visual arts, cultural heritage, arts festivals, museums, music and theater (for example the Klamath Independent Film Festival). The foundation generally does not support conferences, conventions or stand-alone events, so frame requests around programming. Only 501(c)(3) public charities (and occasionally government entities) in the service area. Arts cycle dates for 2027 are not posted; check the foundation page.

name: Creative Expression Grants (folding into Career-Connected Learning in 2027)
contact: Melissa Dubois Lewis, program officer (see pgefoundation.org)

geography.region: Portland General Electric service area (Portland metro, Salem, Willamette Valley)

opens: 2027: pillar folds into Career-Connected Learning; check for the 2027 window
notes: Arts and culture programs that build critical thinking and self-efficacy in youth, for 501(c)(3) nonprofits in PGE's service area. The 2026 round operated at a narrowed scope and from 2027 the pillar is folded into Career-Connected Learning, so arts events should be framed around youth learning outcomes. One request per organization per year.

name: Events and Sponsorships

geography.region: OnPoint's Oregon and southwest Washington service area (Portland metro, Willamette Valley, Central Oregon)

award: Typically $100 to $10,000
opens: Apply at least 90 days before the event start date
notes: Event sponsorships for nonprofits whose programs fit OnPoint's Economic Opportunity and Community Vitality focus (financial wellness, small business, workforce, essential needs, youth education). Requires 501(c)(3), school, foundation or fiscal sponsor status; one event sponsorship per organization per rolling 12 months. OnPoint also awards about $500,000 a year in community grants.

name: Grants, Donations and Sponsorships

geography.region: Communities with a First Interstate Bank branch in Oregon

award: Grants from $2,500 (no stated maximum); donations and sponsorships have no minimum
opens: Requests reviewed monthly; apply online once
notes: Grants require 501(c)(3) or government status and a local branch recommendation; donations and sponsorships are open to organizations without 501(c)(3) status, so for-profit event producers can request sponsorships. Arts and culture and civic/community are stated funding areas. Each market has a Philanthropy Champion who reviews local requests.

name: Community Grant

geography.region: Counties where Umpqua Bank has a retail presence (most of western and central Oregon)

award: Not published; 2024 median $6,000 (range $2,500 to $150,000)
opens: Annual application window; 2026-27 dates not published
notes: Direct-service programs serving majority low-to-moderate-income populations; arts and culture is listed under Healthy Communities. Event sponsorships, operating support and sports/recreation are excluded, so only arts programs with LMI service fit. One application per calendar year. Confirm the current window on the bank's site.

name: Sponsorship Program

geography.region: Portland metro and Port of Portland communities

award: Not published
opens: Submit through portofportland.smapply.us at any time
notes: The Port sponsors events, programs and activities that build vibrant communities around its airport and marine facilities. Applicant type is not restricted on the page; submit a request through the online sponsorship form well ahead of the event. Award sizes are not published.

name: Oregon 250 Grant Program
award: Up to $5,000; more than $244,000 awarded to about 80 organizations
opens: Four funding rounds completed; no open round posted
notes: Funded festivals, parades, lecture series, exhibits and community celebrations commemorating the U.S. 250th anniversary in 2026. All four rounds are complete and the program shows as expired; included only in case a final 2026-27 round is announced.

name: Siletz Tribal Charitable Contribution Fund

geography.region: 11-county service area in western Oregon; also Native American projects anywhere in the U.S.

award: Typically $5,000 to $6,500; no set minimum or maximum
opens: Quarterly; apply one to two weeks before each deadline (2027 dates PDF on site)
notes: Funds projects, activities and events in arts, cultural activities, historic preservation, education and other charitable purposes within the 11-county service area, or projects serving at least 51% Native American participants anywhere. Proof of 501(c)(3) status is not required and local governments may apply. Events must occur after the quarterly distribution date; an evaluation with receipts is due within a year.

name: General Purpose Grants (Small and Large)
funder: Spirit Mountain Community Fund (Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde)
contact: 503-879-1400; 9615 Grand Ronde Rd, Grand Ronde, OR 97347

geography.region: Northwest Oregon (11 counties); government agencies only in Lane, Polk, Tillamook and Yamhill

award: Small grants up to $7,500; large grants up to $50,000 (programs) or $100,000 (capital); request may not exceed 50% of project budget
opens: Quarterly cycles; letter of inquiry then invited application; grant workshop Nov 5, 2026
match: Request cannot exceed 50% of total project budget
notes: Six percent of Spirit Mountain Casino revenue funds 501(c)(3) nonprofits in 11 northwest Oregon counties, plus the nine Oregon tribes. Priorities are health, education, social needs and quality of life; arts and cultural projects have been funded. Two-step quarterly process (LOI, then invitation). Only one open grant at a time; projects must start within 90 days of award.

name: Wildhorse Foundation Grants
funder: Wildhorse Foundation (Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation)

geography.region: Umatilla, Morrow, Union and Wallowa counties, OR, plus the tribes' ceded territory in Benton, Columbia and Walla Walla counties, WA

award: Requests generally up to $30,000 per year; quarterly rounds total about $350,000 to $500,000
opens: Quarterly rounds; the next quarterly deadline falls in early 2027 (confirm exact date on the foundation site)
notes: Funds arts, cultural activities, historic preservation, education, public health and safety and other charitable purposes for nonprofits, government and tribal organizations in the four-county homeland area and the Washington ceded territory. Rapid Response grants are also available. Quarterly deadlines; 12-month grant period.

name: Coquille Tribal Community Fund
contact: Sam Black, 541-756-0904 ext. 1212, 1340 N Bayshore Dr, Coos Bay, OR 97420

geography.region: Coquille Tribe service area in southwestern Oregon (Coos Bay, Bandon and surrounding counties; confirm on the eligibility page)

award: $1,000 and up (requests of $500 or less go to a separate small-donations fund); over $500,000 awarded annually
notes: Annual community grant cycle from the tribe's casino revenue for community groups and nonprofits making lasting contributions in its southwest Oregon service area; awards are presented at a celebration each February. The 2026/27 cycle opened Sept 21 and closes Nov 16, 2026. Small donations and in-kind requests go through separate channels.

name: Cow Creek Umpqua Indian Foundation Grants
contact: Call foundation staff before applying (numbers on guidelines page)

geography.region: Seven counties in southwestern and central Oregon

opens: Deadlines March 1 and September 1 each year
notes: Funds basic needs, abuse prevention and education including arts education and positive youth development for 501(c)(3) nonprofits in seven counties (local governments only in Douglas County). Sports, special events and one-time programming are explicitly excluded, so only ongoing youth arts programs fit. No fiscal agents; one proposal per year.

name: Three Rivers Foundation Grants
funder: Three Rivers Foundation (Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Indians)

geography.region: Coos, Curry, Douglas, Lane and Lincoln counties (plus Harney and Multnomah in the 2025 round); statewide Native-focused projects

opens: Recent cycles opened April 1 with an April 30 deadline; 2027 dates not posted
notes: Three Rivers Casino's foundation funds education, health, public safety, the arts, cultural activities, historic preservation and community enrichment for 501(c)(3) nonprofits, local governments and tribes in its south coast and Lane/Lincoln county area. One open grant at a time; no multi-year requests. Watch for the spring application window.

name: Bend Foundation Grants

geography.region: Bend and Central Oregon

award: Typically $5,000 to $100,000; median about $15,000
opens: Two windows each year: January 5 to March 5 and May 18 to July 17; decisions about seven weeks after close
notes: Supports public art, cultural and educational enrichment and environmental enhancement in Bend. Conferences, events and ongoing operations are not funded, so this fits capital or program components (stages, public art, equipment) rather than event costs. Online form is only live during the two windows.

name: Visitor Experience Grants

geography.region: Portland Region as defined by Travel Oregon

opens: 2026 cycle opened Jan 5, 2026; 2027 cycle not yet posted
match: None required; additional cash or in-kind funds may receive preference
notes: Funded by Portland lodging taxes and administered as Travel Portland's Regional Cooperative Tourism Program investment. Pays for tourism infrastructure, physical enhancements, accessibility and wayfinding. Events, activations under eight weeks, marketing campaigns and salaries are excluded, so this suits permanent festival infrastructure, not event production. Nonprofits, for-profit tourism businesses and tribes may apply.

name: Large Event Sponsorships

geography.region: City of Portland, priority for central city neighborhoods

award: Up to $30,000 depending on event size
opens: Reviewed biannually: applications due April 15 for events in the following July to December and October 15 for events in January to June
notes: Cash sponsorships for public events held in Portland for at least two years, lasting two or more consecutive days, with expected attendance of 7,500 or more and at least 10% out-of-town attendees, that drive leisure demand and show a commitment to equity and accessibility. The page does not restrict applicant type, so for-profit producers may apply. The biannual pattern (April 15 and October 15) is stated; confirm the 2026-27 table on the site.

name: Cultural Enrichment Sponsorships

geography.region: Portland metro area

award: Up to $2,500 or 15% of the event budget, whichever is less
opens: Reviewed biannually on the same April 15 / October 15 schedule as Large Event Sponsorships
notes: Small sponsorships for annual cultural celebrations, festivals, awareness events and fundraisers run by 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) organizations (or fiscally sponsored events) that primarily serve multicultural, women, LGBTQIA2S+, unhoused or accessibility-needs communities in the Portland metro. Event must be at least two years old and open to the public; for-profits are not eligible. Limited number of awards per fiscal year.

name: Scale Up Grant
funder: Prosper Portland Office of Events and Film with Travel Portland

geography.region: City of Portland

award: Three years of funding plus technical assistance and marketing for up to six events per year; $175,000 in the May 2026 round

deadlines.label: Spring 2026 round (awardees announced May 20, 2026; exact deadline not posted)

opens: Next cycle expected spring 2027
notes: Competitive program for Portland events positioned to grow and draw attendees from outside the metro region; winners get multi-year grants and marketing support from Prosper Portland and Travel Portland. 2026 awardees include Vanport Jazz Festival, Portland Jigsaw Masters and Portland Criterium; earlier recipients include Portland's Folk Festival and White Lotus Summer Market. Applicant type is not restricted on the page.

name: Uniquely Portland Event Grant
funder: Prosper Portland Office of Events and Film

geography.region: Event venue must be within the City of Portland; producer may be based in Multnomah, Clackamas, Washington or Clark (WA) county

award: $500 to $7,500 depending on event size and proximity to small businesses; 2026 awards were $800 to $6,000 ($103,910 to 35 events)
opens: Application window opens 120 days and closes 45 days before the event date
notes: Grants for free, all-ages public events in Portland with 300 to 7,500 attendees that drive foot traffic to nearby small businesses. Producers must have produced two successful public events in the last five years; business promotions, political and religious events are excluded. Taxable (1099-G issued). Recipients in 2026 included the 82nd Avenue of Roses Parade ($4,500), Juneteenth Oregon Festival ($6,000), Irish Festival ($6,000) and St. Johns Bizarre ($4,000). Confirm the program is funded for FY2026-27 before applying.

name: Vibrant Districts Grant

geography.region: Portland business districts

award: Up to $10,000 per applicant; Business District Events category up to $5,000; Marketing up to $2,500
opens: 2026 window was Sept 14 to Oct 12; projects complete by June 30, 2027
notes: Only nonprofit business district associations, Neighborhood Prosperity Network districts, enhanced service districts or qualifying neighborhood associations may apply, so event producers partner with their district. Funds free, all-ages signature district events (permits, vendors, insurance, rentals, marketing) plus public space and staffing. Food, alcohol, equipment purchases and retroactive costs are ineligible.

name: Strategic Investment Fund
funder: Experience Mt. Hood and the Gorge (Mt. Hood and Columbia River Gorge Regional Tourism Alliance)

geography.region: Travel Oregon's Mt. Hood and Columbia River Gorge region (Hood River, Wasco and Sherman counties plus the Mt. Hood and Gorge portions of Clackamas and Multnomah counties)

opens: 2026 cycle opened Feb 23; 2027 cycle expected on a similar late-winter schedule
notes: Regional Cooperative Tourism Program funds for one-time, regionally impactful tourism projects; 2026 preferred tourism-related public infrastructure and visitor experience improvements. For-profits may apply only for projects benefiting multiple entities with partner support letters; local DMOs are ineligible. Fifty percent paid up front, balance on completion; projects complete by June 2027. Email application in one message.

name: Strategic Investment Fund

geography.region: Willamette Valley: Yamhill, Marion, Polk, Linn, Benton, non-coastal Lane and southwest Clackamas counties

award: $5,000 to $50,000 per project plus up to 10% administration; $95,176 pool this cycle
notes: Funds destination marketing for shoulder and off-season visitation, destination development (niche experiences, accessibility, trails) and bid-fee support for multi-day sports and meeting events. Event sponsorships, staffing, operations and fundraising are not funded, so position a festival request as off-season marketing or a sports bid. Open to nonprofits, visitor-facing for-profit businesses, tribes and local governments; DMOs may act as fiscal agents. 90% paid up front after MOU; projects complete by Dec 31, 2027.

name: Strategic Investment Fund: Public Art (and invite-only Tribal Tourism)

geography.region: Oregon Coast (coastal portions of Lane and Douglas counties)

award: Not published

deadlines.label: 2026-27 Public Art applications accepted on a rolling basis until this date or until funds are allocated

notes: OCVA's 2026-27 Strategic Investment Fund has two tracks: Public Art (murals, sculpture, interpretive and cultural heritage art), open to coastal nonprofits, tribes, governments and businesses on a rolling basis from July 1, 2026 to May 30, 2027; and Tribal Tourism (planning, signage, exhibits, cultural events), by invitation to tribes and partners. Earlier SIF cycles funded accessibility, events and marketing more broadly, so check for additional tracks.

name: Strategic Partnership Fund

geography.region: Southern Oregon region (Jackson, Josephine, Klamath, Lake and Douglas counties)

award: $2,000 to $15,000 (FY2025-26 awards); $77,000 invested across 12 partners
opens: Annual fiscal-year program; FY2026-27 application dates not posted (guidelines linked from the program page)
notes: Timely support for high-value destination development or marketing projects: accessibility, niche and off-season marketing, outdoor recreation, dark-sky products and destination stewardship. Events have been funded (Savor Southern Oregon, Sarcasm Festival, Storytown Ashland). Open to regional nonprofits, tribes and private businesses located in and serving Southern Oregon. Contact TSO for the current cycle.

recent_recipients.name: Friends of Lake of the Woods

name: Central Oregon Future Fund
funder: Visit Central Oregon (administered by Rural Prosperity Partners)

geography.region: Central Oregon (Deschutes, Jefferson and Crook counties and the Warm Springs Reservation)

award: Requests of approximately $10,000 to $50,000 encouraged; prior rounds totaled about $840,000
match: Not required; at least 10% cash match earns priority points
notes: Regional Cooperative Tourism Program fund for projects that create, protect or preserve a tourism asset under three pillars: Sustainability, Cultural Tourism (with priority for non-peak season, Oct 1 to the Friday before Memorial Day, and rural communities) and Access Adventure. Nonprofits, private businesses, tribes and municipalities may apply; multi-jurisdiction projects earn priority. Awards notified April 2, 2027, funds released April 30, 2027, 12-month project period.

name: EO Regional Grant

geography.region: Eastern Oregon (Travel Oregon's Eastern Oregon region)

award: Not published in the summary; see 2026-27 guidelines

deadlines.label: Revisions due for applicants who requested staff feedback

opens: 2026 window Sept 21 to Oct 26; awards notified Jan 21, 2027; next cycle expected fall 2027
notes: Funds projects that drive visitation and overnight stays or develop destination products tied to EOVA's pillars (Outdoor Recreation, Culture and Heritage, Culinary and Agritourism), including marketing projects with a distribution plan. Applications go through EOVA's grantinterface.com portal; optional staff feedback Nov 6 with revisions due Dec 4, 2026. Applicant types are not restricted on the page; confirm in the guidelines.

name: Tualatin Valley Inspiration Event Award
funder: Explore Tualatin Valley (Washington County Visitors Association)

geography.region: Washington County

award: Up to $5,000 per award for event marketing; up to $25,000 per cycle

deadlines.label: Fall cycle for events Nov 2025 to May 2026 (passed)
Spring cycle for events June to Oct 2026 (passed)

opens: Two windows per fiscal year: July 1 to September 30 and February 1 to April 30 (confirm current-year dates with ETV)
notes: Marketing sponsorships for visitor-facing, public, ADA-compliant events in Washington County, with priority for multi-day, off-season events that generate overnight stays. Washington County-based 501(c) nonprofits, tribes and government partners are eligible; meetings, galas, fundraisers and camps are not. One sponsorship per organization per fiscal year. ETV awarded $27,400 to summer 2025 events. Funded from Washington County lodging tax through the DMO.

name: Foundation Grant Award (Strategic Investment Grant)
funder: Explore Tualatin Valley (Washington County Visitors Association)

geography.region: Washington County

award: Up to $20,000 per award; up to $100,000 per fiscal year
opens: Awards announced in February (2025 round awarded $52,000); current cycle dates not posted
notes: Competitive grants for projects that promote the destination and improve quality of life: small capital projects, public art, historic preservation, heritage projects, recreation and trails, signage and wayfinding. Not event production, but suits permanent festival-related assets. Confirm the application window with ETV.

name: Portland Arts Project Grant
funder: Regional Arts and Culture Council (funded by the City of Portland Office of Arts and Culture)

geography.region: City of Portland

notes: Project grants for Portland-based artists, arts organizations and arts-focused businesses (501(c)(3) not required) for programming, presentations, events and new work shared with the public in 2027. Arts Access Fund is for nonprofits and schools serving K-12 students or underserved communities. Organizations receiving City Operating Support cannot apply. Part of the City's Small Grants Program alongside Friends of IFCC and MusicOregon Echo Fund.

name: Arts3C Grant Program (paused)

geography.region: Multnomah and Washington counties (Clackamas excluded in recent cycles)

opens: Fall cycle not scheduled following changes to City of Portland arts funding; last awards April 2024
notes: RACC's former small-grant program for artists, nonprofits, schools and arts businesses headquartered in Multnomah or Washington County. As of September 2026 the page says the next cycle has not been set, so treat as paused; Portland-based applicants should use the Portland Arts Project Grant instead.

name: Washington County Arts Event Sponsorships
funder: Regional Arts and Culture Council (Washington County funds)

geography.region: Washington County

award: $40,000 distributed to 25 summer arts events in FY26 (about $1,600 average)
opens: Spring; check RACC's Opportunity Portal (racc.smapply.org)
notes: Small sponsorships for free summer arts events in Washington County, administered by RACC. Details and the current application window are posted on RACC's grants pages and portal.

name: Operating Support Grants
funder: City of Portland Office of Arts and Culture

geography.region: City of Portland

award: $25,000 to $145,000 per year for two years
opens: Two-year cycle; next round expected summer 2028
notes: Unrestricted operating support for established Portland arts nonprofits with budgets of at least $150,000, three years of Portland programming and at least half of their budget in the arts; fiscal agents not allowed. Arts festivals organized as nonprofits (for example Portland Jazz Festival-type organizations) qualify. Recipients cannot apply to the Small Grants Program in the same year.

name: Community Placemaking Grants

geography.region: Inside Metro's urban growth boundary (Portland metro)

opens: Recent cycles opened in summer with an early-October deadline; check for a 2027 cycle
notes: Arts and culture-based, community-driven placemaking projects, including events, that strengthen connections to place. Nonprofits, community groups with a fiscal sponsor and public agencies with community partners are eligible; businesses are not. A group whose funded project was an event cannot reapply the following year. No match required.

name: East Portland Action Plan Civic Engagement Sponsorship
funder: City of Portland, East Portland Action Plan

geography.region: East Portland (EPAP service area, generally east of 82nd Avenue)

award: Up to $8,000; about $35,000 available
notes: Sponsors community events and projects that increase civic engagement among underrepresented East Portland communities; must address an EPAP action item. Requires 501(c)(3) status or a 501(c)(3) partner and a Webgrants account. Groups funded in the last two fiscal years are ineligible. Funded activities run March 1, 2027 to March 1, 2028.

name: Community Cultural Participation Grant

geography.region: Multnomah County

award: Up to $3,000
opens: Usually opens in late summer with a mid-October deadline
notes: Oregon Cultural Trust coalition grants for community-based cultural events, programs and organizations headquartered in Multnomah County. 501(c)(3) status is not required; LLCs and other incorporated groups with a county EIN may apply, and fiscal sponsors are allowed. Individuals cannot apply. Two consecutive years of funding maximum, then a year off.

name: Cultural Coalition Project Grant

notes: Arts, heritage and humanities projects benefiting Clackamas County residents, completed within the calendar year applied for. Organizations with a Clackamas County address, and individuals or Oregon organizations partnering with county entities, may apply; nonprofit status is stated as not required. Operating costs, food and beverage are not funded. Final report due within 30 days.

Unusually open eligibility: individuals, groups, nonprofits, for-profit businesses, schools and public bodies may apply.

name: Community Arts Project Grant
funder: Lane Arts Council (City of Eugene Cultural Services)

Individuals, collectives and organizations may apply. Lane Arts Council awarded about $63,800 across its three programs in a recent year.

name: Community Arts Operating Grant
funder: Lane Arts Council (City of Eugene Cultural Services)

geography.region: Organizations serving Eugene

award: Up to $5,000
opens: Opens in winter with an early-April deadline
notes: General operating support for small and mid-sized nonprofit community arts organizations serving Eugene; arts must be the core mission with ongoing public programming. For-profits are not eligible. Lane Arts Council also runs an Artist Grant (up to $2,000) on the same schedule.

name: Cultural Grants

notes: Oregon Cultural Trust coalition grants (co-sponsored by Deschutes County) for cultural nonprofits whose projects address the Deschutes Cultural Plan: awareness of local culture, accessible programming, cultural education and capacity building. Program and operating support is allowed.

name: Cultural Coalition Grants

notes: Oregon Cultural Trust coalition funds to support, preserve and protect arts, heritage and humanities programs in Clatsop County. Applicants are 501(c)(3) nonprofits registered with the Oregon Cultural Trust; individuals may apply through a registered nonprofit fiscal agent. A grant-writing workshop is typically offered before the deadline.

name: Cultural Coalition Grants

notes: Oregon Cultural Trust coalition grants for county-wide cultural events, cultural education, heritage documentation, traditional arts and food culture. Individuals living in Tillamook County, nonprofits headquartered there and local government agencies may apply; ongoing operating funds are not granted.

name: Lincoln County Cultural Grants

The same application covers the Mark R. Sponenburgh Memorial Trust. The coalition's website has had certificate problems; confirm by phone.

The coalition has said it especially wants more heritage and humanities applications. Current-year guidelines and deadline are on its website.
